entries.gap: No empirical or physical argument validates the pilot-to-confirmatory residual-risk transport radii.
entries.impact: Width certificates, regret and feasibility labels; not R164 coverage conditional on a selected valid plan.
entries.counterexample: Independent deterministic pilot X=0 and confirmatory X=1 reverse the ranking of centers 0 and 1.
entries.corrected_now: Independence and residual transport are separate nodes; the width theorem requires both menu and transport premises explicitly.
entries.unresolved_premise: Justify or sensitivity-analyse tau_jq for the actual protocol and participant designs.

entries.gap: The declared objective is maximum component expected untruncated half-width, not realized maximum width, decision power or probability of a decisive R161 outcome.
entries.impact: A width-certified plan may still be unresolved or occasionally wide.
entries.counterexample: A bounded residual with small expectation can realize a large confirmatory residual sum on some samples.
entries.corrected_now: The objective and evidence level are typed exactly and no power claim is made.
entries.unresolved_premise: A high-probability realized-width or decision-power criterion needs another frozen theorem and effect scenario.

entries.gap: The finite menu may omit the scientifically best or only feasible plan, and its centers/lambdas have no apparatus-specific justification.
entries.impact: Regret and DESIGN_NOT_FEASIBLE are menu-relative rather than global.
entries.counterexample: A center outside the menu can have zero confirmatory residual while every listed center is poor.
entries.corrected_now: Every result states its finite-menu relativity and deterministic resource envelope.
entries.unresolved_premise: Predeclare a scientifically justified menu before any actual pilot.

entries.gap: Finite pilot uncertainty can leave neither feasibility nor infeasibility certified.
entries.impact: A binary pilot decision would misclassify uncertain cases and invite post-hoc interval switching.
entries.counterexample: In the saved synthetic audit, w_max=.22 lies below every upper certificate but not below every lower certificate.
entries.corrected_now: PILOT_INCONCLUSIVE is mandatory; DESIGN_NOT_FEASIBLE requires every lower certificate above threshold or deterministic resource emptiness.
entries.unresolved_premise: Rules for any new pilot/menu/threshold version must be declared without confirmatory reuse.

entries.gap: Participant-vector independence, gate validity, bounded readout construction, missingness targets and apparatus fidelity remain untested.
entries.impact: Neither coverage nor width certificates have an actual human implementation witness.
entries.counterexample: Coordinated participants or common session disturbances violate the participant-level independence used by the finite-design specialization.
entries.corrected_now: The contracts retain all R161 gates and separate pilot, confirmatory, statistical and actual-organizational objects.
entries.unresolved_premise: Ethically approved apparatus validation and participant-level dependence audit.

entries.gap: The auxiliary statistical design still does not show that a population role profile is an actually installed body-frame relation in one token or that such a relation realizes felt mineness.
entries.impact: No B_min, F_O, complete organization, consciousness criterion or unique owner follows.
entries.counterexample: Two protocols can have identical valid population intervals while differing in whether the measured relation is installed in any participant's operative body-frame organization.
entries.corrected_now: R165 is marked auxiliary and the next question returns to the organization-level bridge rather than extending statistics again.
entries.unresolved_premise: Independently specified token-level physical-role witness and separately justified experience-internal mineness bridge.
